sections.heading: FAQ
blocks: Straight answers, for people and for machines.

Vahid Faraji is a Senior Applied AI Specialist at Kariyer.net (ilab group) in Istanbul, Turkey. He has 9+ years shipping production systems and works at the boundary of research and production, publishing peer-reviewed work at ACM while deploying enterprise-scale multi-agent systems. His focus areas are multi-agent orchestration, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and context engineering for large language models.
What does Vahid Faraji actually build?

Production LLM agent systems for enterprises. Recent work includes an MCP-based multi-agent classification system that reached 95% accuracy on 14,000+ job positions while cutting classification time 72.5% and API calls 41.8%; an enterprise AI platform on LangGraph, MCP and Agno that reduced manual reporting workload 60% for 200+ internal users; and a 300M+ datapoint metadata architecture that became the retrieval and grounding foundation for later LLM deployments.

Three peer-reviewed and preprint papers. “Multi-Agent Position Classification with Tool Orchestration” is peer-reviewed and published in the ACM Digital Library (DOI 10.1145/3786335.3813207), presented at ACM CAIS '26 in San Jose. “Tokalator: A Context Engineering Toolkit for AI Coding Assistants” is on arXiv (2604.08290). “Leveraging LLMs For Turkish Skill Extraction” is on arXiv (2601.22885) and is the first systematic LLM benchmark for Turkish workforce analytics. One patent is pending.

Tokalator is an open-source context engineering toolkit built by Vahid Faraji, shipped as a VS Code extension and a web platform with 500+ installs under an MIT licence. It provides real-time token budgeting, tab relevance scoring, Cobb-Douglas output-quality modelling and caching break-even analysis across 17 LLMs. It is documented at tokalator.wiki and described in arXiv paper 2604.08290.
Which technologies and frameworks does Vahid Faraji work with?

Agent and LLM stack: Model Context Protocol (MCP), LangGraph, Agno, the Anthropic SDK, Vercel AI SDK and Arize for observability. Backend and data: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Text-to-SQL, DataHub, Azure Synapse, BigQuery and real-time pipelines. Frontend and tooling: Next.js, TypeScript and VS Code extension development.
Is Vahid Faraji available to hire or consult?

Yes. For applied AI advisory, agent-system architecture reviews, and enterprise AI training. He is based in Istanbul (GMT+3) and works with distributed teams. The fastest route is to book a call directly on his calendar or email vfaraji89@gmail.com; the site also has a “suggest a time” form that proposes a slot in your own timezone.
Does Vahid Faraji do training and teaching?

Yes. He has trained 400+ people across 50+ courses, including an 18-hour Applied AI programme with Techcareer covering custom tool design, contextual system architecture, multi-agent coordination and production tool execution. He mentors on AI career paths for the TEV Foundation and gives guest lectures on enterprise prompt engineering at Kayseri University and Van University.
What makes an applied AI profile like this different from an ML engineer?

The work is measured in shipped systems and business deltas rather than model metrics alone: accuracy on real taxonomies, latency and API-cost reductions, adoption counts, and workload removed. It spans the full path: problem framing, solution architecture, agent orchestration, evaluation and observability, and the data and metadata layer that makes retrieval trustworthy in the first place.
Where is Vahid Faraji based and what languages does he speak?

Istanbul, Turkey (GMT+3). He speaks Turkish natively, English at C1 level, Spanish at instructor level, and basic Portuguese. He holds an M.A. in Economics from Ibn Haldun University with a thesis on real-time labour market analysis.

sections.heading: How I save 38% on LLM tokens
blocks: A context engineering methodology applied across 16M+ tokens of real production workloads. Not theory, measured results.

sections.heading: 01 The problem
blocks: Most LLM-powered systems treat context as unlimited. They dump full documents, conversation history, and tool outputs into prompts without measuring cost or relevance. The result: token burn, degraded accuracy from context pollution, and unpredictable latency.
Working across enterprise deployments at Kariyer.net across Sales, Finance and R&D, I needed a systematic approach to context that scales.

sections.heading: 02 The methodology
blocks: Five principles, applied together as a system:
Select only the context that directly serves the current task. Score relevance, filter aggressively, and validate that every token in the window earns its place.
Compress conversation history and intermediate outputs before they accumulate. Summarize completed reasoning chains. Retain decisions, discard derivations.
Prevent irrelevant tool outputs, stale cache entries, and redundant instructions from entering the context window. Gate every injection point.
Build context progressively rather than loading everything upfront. Start minimal, expand as needed, compact as you go. Match context lifecycle to task lifecycle.

sections.heading: 03 The infrastructure layer
blocks: Methodology alone isn't enough. You need supporting infrastructure that makes these principles the default, not an afterthought:
Curated, deduplicated, and version-controlled data sources. No stale documents. No conflicting definitions. Every fact traceable to a source.
A shared vocabulary across agents, tools, and humans. Eliminates ambiguity in multi-agent handoffs. Reduces re-explanation tokens to near-zero.
Structured organizational knowledge accessible to agents via RAG. Maintained like code: PRs, reviews, deprecation cycles. Not a document dump.
Model relationships between entities, decisions, and documents as a graph. Agents traverse edges to find relevant context instead of scanning flat text.

sections.heading: 04 Context as a graph
blocks: The core insight: context isn't a flat window, it's a connected graph. Each node carries meaning, each edge carries relevance. Agents navigate the graph to assemble exactly the right context for each step.

sections.heading: 05 Results
blocks: Applied across enterprise LLM deployments at Kariyer.net (100+ internal users), this methodology delivers:
Measured across 16M+ tokens of production workloads. Not cherry-picked benchmarks. Real queries, real users, real cost savings.
Less context pollution means fewer hallucinations. Agents work with relevant, curated context instead of noisy document dumps.
Smaller, targeted context windows mean faster inference. No surprises from bloated prompts hitting rate limits.
Adopted as organizational standard. Documented in Tokalator and published at arXiv:2604.08290.
